data.title: CSS
data.tagline: CSS is a style language that describes a web page's appearance, layout, and changes across available space.
data.learningOutcome: You can inspect matched CSS rules and final computed values from a visible symptom, and distinguish styling from HTML structure or JavaScript behavior.
data.description: For example, HTML may already contain a button while the button is still gray or overflows on a phone. The browser matches CSS rules and calculates a final style from their priority and order. CSS controls presentation; it does not implement the business logic that runs after a click.

learning.assumes: You have seen a page's HTML and encountered a page whose structure is right but whose color, spacing, or layout is wrong.
learning.outcome: You can inspect matched CSS rules and final computed values from a visible symptom, and distinguish styling from HTML structure or JavaScript behavior.

distinctions.label: HTML
distinctions.explanation: HTML describes what the page contains and how it is structured; CSS describes how that structure looks and lays out.

distinctions.label: JavaScript
distinctions.explanation: CSS changes presentation; JavaScript responds to actions and changes behavior or data.

explanation.title: First check which rules match
explanation.text: A selector decides whether a rule applies to an element. AI often generates code with classes like class="card" or utility classes like p-4 and flex in Tailwind, where each class matches specific style rules.

explanation.title: Then see which declaration wins
explanation.text: Matching scope, priority, and source order all affect the result. DevTools Styles and Computed panels show crossed-out declarations and the final value.

data.boundary: CSS controls appearance, layout, and responsive changes; HTML controls content structure, and JavaScript controls interaction behavior. Flex, Grid, and the box model are specific CSS layout concepts, not a second full course here.

lessonPractice.title: The primary button is clickable, but it still appears gray. What should you inspect first?

options.label: Inspect the button's matched CSS rules and computed color to find the override
options.feedback: Correct. The button behavior already exists, so inspect matching and the final value to find where the theme color was replaced.

options.label: Rewrite the click handler so the click also sets the theme color
options.feedback: Click behavior and a static color are separate. This can hide the CSS conflict and make the color depend on one click.

options.label: Replace the button with another HTML element and expect the theme color automatically
options.feedback: Changing the element does not resolve a stylesheet conflict. Check selector matching and which declaration wins first.

data.agentPrompt: Inspect the CSS rules matched by this primary button and its final computed style. Find which gray declaration overrides the theme color. Preserve the HTML structure and click behavior, fix only the styling, and verify the color, layout, and overflow at desktop and 390px widths.
